主要内容: The article discusses 15 U.S. companies with zero debt, emphasizing their cash and short-term investment holdings. These companies are noted for maintaining low debt levels, which allows them to operate without financial strain. The data is sourced from SEC filings, Capital IQ, and Thomson Reuters. The article mentions that only 22 companies in the S&P 500 reported zero debt on their balance sheets. Among these, the top 15 companies are highlighted for their significant cash reserves and short-term investments. The average return for these top 15 firms in the past year was 15%, compared to a 2% gain for the S&P 500. The companies listed include Fastenal (FAST), C.H. Robinson Worldwide (CHRW), F5 Networks (FFIV), Citrix (CTXS), Red Hat (RHT), LSI Corp (LSI), and T Rowe Price Group (TROW). Each company's financial details, including total debt, cash and short-term investments, total assets, and stock performance, are provided. The article also notes that cash holdings do not include long-term investments and that total debt includes various forms of borrowing but excludes all possible liabilities. The article lists 15 companies with zero debt, highlighting their financial health and performance. Autodesk (ADSK) has $1.37 billion in cash and short-term investments, with a cash-to-asset ratio of 46.2%. Bed Bath and Beyond (BBBY) shows strong growth with a 25.76% year-to-date stock price increase. Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) has a high cash-to-asset ratio of 70.9%, indicating strong liquidity. Forest Labs (FRX) and Cognizant Tech (CTSH) also maintain zero debt, with significant cash reserves. Mastercard (MA) and Amazon.com (AMZN) are noted for their robust financial positions, with Amazon having $6.32 billion in cash and short-term investments. Apple (AAPL) stands out with $30.2 billion in cash and short-term investments, despite its large asset base. These companies demonstrate financial stability and strong market performance, making them attractive for investors seeking low-debt, high-liquidity options.
